The silence on the record proves only that no rider message exists (F11); it does not establish the amount charged, and the driver's own closing message "8 min up, cancelling the trip" (F10) shows he terminated the booking himself at 12:25:20 (F4, F5), so the $5.00 on the fare record (F7) is left unexplained by NS-1/NS-2.

Accepted — there is no GPS gap; but a gap-free record of waiting is exactly what defeats their own pricing argument, because it shows a completed wait on a trip that was never completed by the rider (F3, F6, F4), and NS-6 requires a completed trip with an in-trip drop-off tap for any $5.00 waiting charge.

F12 is a post-trip written statement, not part of the chat record (F11); it is consistent only with the waiting point, which I concede, and it says nothing that satisfies NS-6's completed-trip and drop-off-tap conditions, which the driver's own cancellation record (F4, F5) rules out.

This is the crux and it fails: NS-0 permits only the $6.61 cancellation fee for a no-show branch and NS-6 permits the $5.00 waiting fee only where the rider boarded and the trip was completed, and the fare record shows $5.00 (F7) on a trip the driver cancelled (F4, F5) — no cited clause produces that $5.00, so it must be waived.

I don't need the profile to win, and I do not ask for a flag based on it alone; I simply note that 2 of his 3 ninety-day disputes were upheld no-show findings (F17) while the rider's record shows 0 upheld (F16), which is a reason for Ryde to look, not a substitute for the NS-6 finding.

Agreed, and it is the driver's side of the case: NS-1 (i) and (ii) are satisfied because the driver himself tapped "I'm Here" at 12:17:10 while 39 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m radius (F6).

Agreed on the merits of NS-1 (iii): the driver stayed within 200 m for 8 min 10 s after the tap (F6) and was stationary 8 min 30 s at 41 m from the pickup (F3), so all three NS-1 conditions are met and the fee is not defeated by any failure to wait. The rider's residual point - that the charge exists at all - is answered at C5: NS-1, not NS-6, is the clause that authorises a charge on a driver-cancelled no-show.

The label does not move the charge to NS-6: NS-0 makes the no-show branch (NS-1/NS-2) the exclusive route for a driver-cancelled trip, and the $5.00 recorded on the fare record (F7, F4) is the amount actually charged for the rider's no-show; NS-6 governs a waiting fee added at drop-off on a completed trip, which this never was. If the judge holds the recorded amount unexplained, that affects quantum only, not whether a no-show charge was owed.

C5 proves too much for the rider: the absence of a completed trip and of any drop-off tap (F4, F10) is exactly why NS-6 does not apply, and why the charge is assessed under NS-1 instead - the driver arrived, tapped "I'm Here" at 39 m (F6), waited 8 min 10 s in radius (F6, F3) and the rider never appeared (F9, F10, F11), so NS-1 is satisfied and the fee stands.

C6 concedes the decisive facts: the driver announced arrival at 12:17 (F9), cancelled at 12:25 after the wait (F10) on a complete, timestamped record containing no rider reply (F11), while GPS independently shows 9 min 35 s within 200 m (F2) and 8 min 30 s stationary (F3) - that is NS-1 met in full. NS-2 only applies where one of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) fails; none does, so the rider's request for a full refund has no clause to stand on.

The rider is right that a driver's statement cannot substitute for evidence, and I do not rely on F12 for the finding: F5 and F6 do not contradict the driver, they corroborate him - platform arrival at 12:15:25 and a cancellation 9 min 55 s later (F5), with the tap at 12:17:10 and 8 min 10 s in radius afterwards (F6). Both profiles are irrelevant to the finding and the flag request fails: the rider's own record shows zero upheld no-show disputes (F16), and the driver's two upheld matters are no-show matters consistent with this trip's clock evidence - stationary 8 min 30 s at 41 m (F3), 9 min 35 s within 200 m (F2) - so there is nothing fraudulent here to send for review (NS-2's flag attaches only where NS-1 fails, which it does not).
